title: Started forward testing my deterministic multi-strategy portfolio on IBKR paper
author: Vegetable-Warthog81
selftext:
Finally started forward testing this on IBKR paper.

I use AI heavily in the research pipeline, but every actual trading strategy is fully deterministic. I’m not running a single strategy either — the portfolio is built from combinations of relatively orthogonal strategies.

Since the candidate pool is pretty large, I use heuristic optimization to search for good combinations. Mostly working with regular equities and standard market indicators for now, but I’m also thinking about adding a few custom indices of my own.

comments.author: Livid_Parsnip_2816
comments.body: Very similar direction here, just in MT5 and FX. Anduril runs pair-specific deterministic modules under one portfolio layer. One live session this week closed 6 trades across 5 pairs, all positive. Way too small to mean anything statistically, but it was a useful check that the modules and portfolio controls behaved together. How are you measuring orthogonality?

replies.author: Vegetable-Warthog81
replies.body:
Similar idea, though each of my strategies already includes ranking the candidate universe and fractional allocation. I then combine those strategy-level portfolios using daily return correlation over the backtest period, with heuristic search over 10k+ candidates.

One thing I’m still trying to understand is why some combinations that look well protected against overfitting/lookahead leakage and also have low correlation can still fail OOS. It only happens occasionally, and my OOS window is still under 3 months, so it may be too early to read much into it — but I’m curious what I might be missing.

replies.author: Livid_Parsnip_2816
replies.body: Under three months I’d be careful blaming the selection process yet. Low pairwise correlation can still hide the same regime exposure, so I also look at correlation during losing periods, overlapping market exposure and contribution to portfolio drawdown. Two strategies can look independent overall and still fail together when volatility changes. With Anduril I use rolling correlation plus removal and stress tests at portfolio level. I’d freeze this selection and let the OOS window grow before changing it.

replies.author: Vegetable-Warthog81
replies.body: This is genuinely useful advice. I think you’re right — I’ve probably been treating correlation too simplistically. As long as it doesn’t blow up my compute, I’ll make the correlation analysis more elaborate, especially in stress/losing regimes. Thanks.
